_doc: v3 happy path: create a generic project, start a run, expect it to reach `paused` after brief_intake (a local-only stage with no LLM/downstream-service dependency). Validates: license-token auth, /api/projects create, /api/deliverables/{id}/runs dispatch, single-stage execution, and the pause-after-stages mechanism.

brief.audience: solo founders filing their own accounts

_assert_doc: expect_terminal_status alone proved only that the run STOPPED, not that anything reached the stage. This is a nightly-core scenario, so that was the primary nightly signal. brief_intake defaults title to 'Untitled' and target_duration_seconds to 60 when the brief does not arrive, so equality against the values set above goes red if config_snapshot is dropped or the brief is not threaded through. Only brief_intake is assertable here: the run pauses after it, so no render stage ever executes and there is no artifact to check.
_strengthened_2026_09_05:
TWO changes, both about assertions that could not fail.

(1) TERMINAL. Was ["paused", "completed"]. This scenario's stated purpose is to validate the pause-after-stages mechanism, and accepting `completed` accepted the exact failure it exists to catch: the generic blueprint has stages AFTER brief_intake (stages/generic/: script_draft, narrate, video_render), so a run that reaches `completed` with pause_after_stages=["brief_intake"] means the gate did NOT hold. Narrowed to ["paused"], matching every other pausing spec in the suite (demo_video_gen_happy_path, demo_video_claim_finish).

(2) DISCRIMINATING BRIEF VALUES. brief_intake (stages/generic/brief_intake.py:43-50) is a pure projection of config_snapshot — every one of its six output fields is `cfg/brief/voice.get(key, <default>)`, so there is no produced output here to assert on, only threading. That makes the DEFAULTS the whole game: angle defaulted to 'informational', audience to 'general' and voice.descriptor to 'neutral', and this brief had POSTed exactly those three strings — so an `equals` on any of them would have passed just as well against a DROPPED brief/voice block. They are now set to values no default can produce, which turns three vacuous fields into three real ones. `voice_descriptor` in particular is the only check covering the `voice` block, a different top-level snapshot key from `brief`. The pre-existing title/target_duration_seconds checks are KEPT: they were already discriminating (defaults 'Untitled' / 60) and are cheap.
